_readme: Durable manual split corrections for price_cache/*.parquet.
Why this file exists: Yahoo's own split table is missing certain reverse
splits (see split_fingerprint.py's docstring). auto_adjust=True cannot
back-adjust a split Yahoo does not know happened, so any fix applied
directly to a cached parquet file gets silently destroyed the next time
backtest/prices.py re-fetches that ticker -- confirmed 2026-08-07 when a
hand-applied DKI fix was overwritten by a routine backtest run.
This file is the durable source of truth instead. backtest/prices.py
(see apply_price_overrides in price_overrides.py) re-applies every entry
below to a ticker's frame on every load AND every fetch, so no re-fetch
can lose the correction again. Each entry independently checks whether
the raw jump it describes is still present before adjusting -- see
price_overrides.py:_jump_present -- so an already-corrected frame (or a
ticker Yahoo has since fixed itself) is left alone rather than
double-adjusted.
price_ratio is the raw overnight close ratio (close[date] /
close[previous bar]) for a reverse split, matching split_fingerprint.py's
SplitEvent.price_ratio convention. observed_volume_ratio and
observed_dollar_volume_ratio are recorded for provenance only (they are
not re-validated on load); they are the median-window volume fingerprint
values split_fingerprint.detect_unadjusted_splits computed against the
cache at the time each entry was added.

overrides.why: Yahoo's split table is missing this 1-for-16.7 reverse split. Confirmed by the price/volume fingerprint: close 0.336 -> 5.610 (16.696x) while volume 636,700 -> 68,900 (0.108x) on the adjacent bars, dollar volume roughly preserved (1.81x). Falls below split_fingerprint.py's MIN_PRE_JUMP_DOLLAR_VOLUME tradeability floor (pre-jump ~$214k median-window dollar volume < $500k), so the automated --scan does not surface it as 'split' on its own; this entry is the confirmed manual override the automated scan would otherwise miss. A hand-applied fix to the parquet was overwritten by a re-fetch on 2026-08-07, which is the incident that prompted this override mechanism.
